name: Curious
blurb: New things, tried together. Kink exploration for two curious people.

cards.text: The Try-New-Things menu: each writes three things you're curious to explore with me — one gentle, one bold, one wild card. Trade. Pick one to order this month.
cards.soften: Say one thing you're curious about, no list.

cards.text: Blindfold them (scarf, shirt, sleep mask). Five minutes of your undivided attention — you decide everything, gently.
cards.speak: Narrate what you're about to do before you do it. Always.
cards.soften: Eyes closed, one minute of touch, narrated.

cards.text: Power swap: one of you gives a single, gentle command; the other follows for three minutes. Then swap. Safe word exists and is sacred.
cards.soften: Just trade: each names one thing you'd want the other to take the lead on.

cards.text: Ice trace: run an ice cube slowly along their collarbone and neck. Your other hand is not allowed to help.
cards.soften: Feather-light fingertip trace instead of ice.

cards.text: What's a fantasy you've never said out loud? The card swears confidentiality — what happens in Ember stays in Ember.
The tease game: whoever gives in and touches the other first loses, and grants one wish tonight. No time limit — that's the point.
cards.soften: Ten seconds of almost-touching, then swap.

cards.text: Take control of their evening for the next hour: pick the next two cards, the music, and how close they sit.
cards.soften: Take control of just the next card.

cards.text: Trade answers: what does 'being wanted' feel like for you — chased, chosen, claimed, or something else entirely?
Tell them one new sensation you've been quietly curious to try together and what draws you to it.
Share a light power-exchange idea that makes you curious — either leading or following for a short stretch.
Describe a texture, temperature, or soft object you'd love to explore on each other's skin someday.
What is one pacing or teasing game you've imagined that keeps both of you on the edge of wanting more?
Name one brand-new experience you'd like to invent together just because it sounds fun to discover.
Invite them to close their eyes or use a soft blindfold while you slowly introduce three different gentle textures or temperatures across their skin.
cards.speak: Feel this one… now this… tell me which makes you shiver.
cards.soften: Ask them to close their eyes and let you trail one soft scarf or your fingertips slowly.

cards.text: Offer to take the lead for the next ten minutes: choose the pace, the touches, and the moments of pause while they simply receive.
cards.speak: Just follow me for these ten minutes. I've got you.
cards.soften: Ask if you can guide the next few minutes of closeness and check in after.

cards.text: Invite them into a no-touch tease: stay close enough to feel each other's breath and describe, in detail, exactly what you would do if touching were allowed.
cards.speak: If I could touch you right now I'd start here and take my time…
cards.soften: Sit close and share one soft, detailed description of a touch you'd like to give.

cards.text: Offer a feather, ice cube, or soft fabric and invite them to explore your skin with it however curiosity leads for one full minute.
cards.speak: Show me what feels good. I'm curious too.
cards.soften: Hand them a soft scarf and invite a few slow strokes across your arm or back.

cards.text: Invite them to blindfold you gently, then narrate every soft thing you're feeling while they use only light texture or temperature play.
cards.speak: That feels cool… now warmer… keep going, I want to notice everything.
cards.soften: Close your eyes and simply describe the first gentle touch they offer.

cards.text: Propose a short follow-the-leader round: they set a slow rhythm of kisses or touches and you match it exactly for sixty seconds.
cards.soften: Ask them to set a gentle pace of kisses and follow along for a short while.

cards.text: Invite them to hover their hands just above your skin and move them slowly so you can feel the heat without contact for a full minute.
cards.speak: I can feel you right there. Don't touch yet.
cards.soften: Sit close with hands near each other and notice the warmth for twenty seconds.

cards.text: Offer to build a tiny sensory station with whatever is nearby (ice, fabric, feather, warm breath) and invite them to choose the order.
cards.soften: Gather two soft things and let them pick which one you use first.

cards.text: Invite them to take your hands and guide them wherever curiosity points for thirty seconds while you keep your eyes closed.
cards.speak: Show me. I'm open to whatever you want me to feel.
cards.soften: Close your eyes and let them place your hands somewhere gentle.

cards.text: Propose a pacing game: kiss or touch for ten seconds, pause for ten, repeat three times, letting the want build.
cards.soften: Share three slow kisses with a short breath between each.

cards.text: Invite them to describe, out loud, one new way they'd like to be touched while you listen without acting on it yet.
cards.soften: Ask them to share one soft new idea for closeness and simply thank them.

cards.text: Together, each build a short 'try-new-things' menu of three curious ideas (sensory, pacing, or light lead/follow). Share the menus, then circle one item you both want to explore soon.
cards.soften: Each name one new gentle idea you'd like to try and pick a favorite together.

cards.text: Take turns leading for three minutes each: the leader chooses only soft sensory play (texture, temperature, breath) while the other simply receives and notices.
cards.soften: Take turns offering one minute of gentle, curious touch while the other relaxes.

cards.text: Create a shared tease-without-touching game: sit close, keep hands to yourselves, and take turns saying one specific thing you'd do if touch were allowed, building the list together.
cards.soften: Sit close and each share one soft description of a touch you'd like to give.

cards.text: Talk about the difference between 'curious' and 'ready' and how you both like to signal when something new feels exciting.
Share the softest or most surprising sensory idea either of you has ever wanted to try with the other.
Discuss how it feels when one of you takes the lead for a little while and what makes that feel safe and fun.
